dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But written words tend to last a little longer, don't they?

dialogues.speaker: Mengzhou
dialogues.text: And what good does that do? Once something is written down, it becomes a dead thing. As time passes, the interpretations get twisted, until all you're left with at last is a handful of ignorant descendants coming to blows over the meaning of a word or two.

dialogues.speaker: Mengzhou
dialogues.text: Tsk. Better to just make up stories. At least no one would take them for the truth.
